articles.body: The Detroit Lions have recorded a pretty strong ru on the field this season as the team has lost only 2 games so far against the Carolina Panthers and the Buffalo Bills. But the team faced a major setback when defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season ending torn ACL in his right knee during the first quarter of Sunday's game. Amid all the mess, he has penned an emotional note which has sparked a debate.Aidan Hutchinson’s emotional note about his injury sparks a heated debate among fansA few hours ago, the Detroit Lions’ star player Aidan Hutchinson took to his social media to make a post that read as, “honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won’t hold me back. I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense.”The star defensive end added, “All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him. Very grateful for all of your prayers and well wishes. Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger. 2. That’s the last time I go airborne 😁👍 Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys.”But this has not gone down well with fans; a fan wrote, “Bad karma by Hutchinson..celebrated ending Maye’s season in a place where if the Patriots hadn’t beat Munich in the 1940’s we would all be speaking German right now.”Another fan posted, “Breaking. God knows why. You did stupid selfish sh*t. Team first. Celebrate your team mates efforts and successes they worked hard. Not your own. Simple.”Another fan commented, ““Only God knows” God also knows how much pain he caused my for tackling Maye in the dirtiest way possible to screw my out of the LA GAME in 2 weeks.”A fourth fan noted, “he’s talking about how he needs to lean on his faith for this “random” injury just don’t land w/ both legs out like that. it’s not complicated. give your knees room to give so the energy from the jump goes elsewhere fans have been begging him to stop jumping like that for years.”However, Aidan Hutchinson has not responded to the comments yet as he remains focused on recovery.What really happened to Aidan Hutchinson at the clash against the New England Patriots?Aidan Hutchinson sacked Patriots quarterback Drake Maye on third down in the first quarter and was spotted celebrating it.After getting up, Aidan Hutchinson jumped into the air and pumped his right fist as he ended up landing awkwardlyon his right leg, which buckled under him. He immediately grabbed his right knee, remained on the ground, and later walked off under his own power to the blue medical tent and locker roomGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chris Simms bought a $4.5 million New York City home weeks after selling his 300-year-old Connecticut farmhouse for $5.5 million; inside the former NFL quarterback’s latest property move
articles.summary: Chris Simms bought a 3,700 sq-ft Connecticut farmhouse in 2019 for $2.5 million.
articles.body: Chris Simms bought a 3,700 sq-ft Connecticut farmhouse in 2019 for $2.5 million. The property carries a piece of Greenwich history coupled with modern mansion luxury. The five-bedroom, five-bathroom dwelling was originally built in 1725; it underwent extensive restoration and renovation before Chris Simms and his wife, Danielle, occupied it in 2019.The couple listed the Greenwich abode for $8 million in February. Within months, they dropped the asking price by $500,000. Then, in June, they made a second price cut of $600,000. Just two months later, in August, a third discount further lowered the asking price to $6.2 million.The NFL analyst for NBC Sports eventually found a buyer for his 300-year-old Connecticut farmhouse after having settled for $5.5 million in November. Weeks later, the former NFL quarterback bought a plush property in the tallest tower in New York City’s East Side for $4.5 million.Chris Simms not only saved money on his current Sutton Tower home purchase [$1 million profit compared to his Connecticut sale] but also profited from his Greenwich sale [$3 million profit compared to his initial purchase in 2019]. So technically speaking, he profited $4 million from his latest property move.Chris Simms’ Connecticut farmhouse“Being the steward of this [Connecticut farmhouse] remarkable home and property has been a true privilege,” the Simmses told Robb Report via an email. “Our family has shared so many unforgettable moments here, from leisurely trail rides with our horses throughout the neighborhood to enchanting holiday celebrations in the historic barn.”Before buying this Greenwich property in 2019, Chris Simms and wife Danielle sold their previous home in the neighborhood for little less than $2.7 million. The Simmses purchased the second Connecticut farmhouse because they wanted more space and room for horses. The Greenwich property includes three horse stalls with a tack room and three paddocks.The nearly 3,700 sq. ft. home has six bedrooms and five full bathrooms. The property boasts a large main level with plenty of gathering space. The living room, family room, and media room feature wide-plank antique floors and exposed wood beams. Preserved brick fireplaces add a warm traditional touch to those rooms.A modern kitchen features state-of-the-art appliances, a white marble island, white cabinetry, and a nearby dining room for easy serving to guests and family.The main floor also has a primary suite with cathedral ceilings in the bedroom and bathroom, including a bespoke dressing room and a private staircase to a quiet, light-filled office and library retreat for everyday living. Large floor-to-ceiling windows offer mesmerizing meadow views outside.The lower level of the farmhouse features a recreation room and a gym. Outside, four acres of land were dedicated to horse care. The historic barn was turned into a party space. An additional pool house comes with its own kitchenette.“The residence blends historic authenticity with modern luxury, featuring original architectural details,” the listing says. “The property has direct access to the Greenwich Riding Trails.”Chris Simms’ New York City homeChris Simms recently purchased a stunning residence in Sutton Tower of New York City for $4.5 million. Sutton Tower is an 847-ft limestone tower designed by Danish architect Thomas Juul-Hansen. The tower was built in 2022 and is the tallest on the East Side waterfront.The building boasts a 9,100 sq-ft, $65 million penthouse at the 80th and 81st floors. The plush five-bedroom penthouse offers tranquil water and cityscape views.Building amenities include a lap pool, a personal training studio, infrared saunas, a spa and treatment room, and a gym. The tower’s two floors are designed for entertaining and recreation, including a lounge, a terrace, and a private dining room.The New York Post reported that Kristen Suh and Loretta Shanahan of Corcoran Sunshine Marketing Group were listing brokers for the Sutton Tower. Chris Simms’ broker was Monica Webster of Douglas Elliman. She also listed Simms’ Greenwich property.Chris Simms’ new apartment is located on an undisclosed high floor in the building. It comes with three bedrooms, three-and-a-half bathrooms, and floor-to-ceiling windows offering peaceful panoramic views.The apartment begins with an entry gallery that leads into the living room and dining area. Both the living room and dining area offer skyline views. The apartment also features a chef’s kitchen and a main bedroom suite with ample closet space.Carrying some memory from his Connecticut property, the retired NFL quarterback made sure the flooring design detail included 5–inch–wide oak plank floors. His Greenwich property boasted wide-plank antique floors and exposed wood beams.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joe Burrow, Jahmyr Gibbs Eyed for NFL Awards in New Poll of Execs Ahead of Week 11
articles.summary: Just beyond the midway point of the 2026 NFL regular season, Joe Burrow has emerged as the clear MVP frontrunner to executives across the league.
articles.body:
Just beyond the midway point of the 2026 NFL regular season, Joe Burrow has emerged as the clear MVP frontrunner to executives across the league.

In a survey of 27 talent evaluators, including general managers and directors of player personnel, conducted by Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer , Burrow received 22 votes for MVP.

Josh Allen was the only other player to receive multiple MVP votes with two. Jahmyr Gibbs, Brock Purdy and Kenneth Walker III all received one vote.

The Offensive Player of the Year ballot was much closer, with Gibbs topping the list at 12 to beat out Jaxon Smith-Njigba with eight. Burrow (three), Ja'Marr Chase (three) and Walker (one) received the remaining votes.

Other award leaders at this point in the season include Will Anderson Jr. (Defensive Player of the Year), Denzel Boston (Offensive Rookie of the Year), Arvell Reese (Defensive Rookie of the Year), Kyle Shanahan (Coach of the Year) and John Lynch (Executive of the Year).

Burrow is coming off an absurd two-game stretch against the Atlanta Falcons and Pittsburgh Steelers in which he completed 59 of 73 attempts (80.8 percent) for 680 yards, seven touchdowns and no interceptions.

The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback has thrown at least three touchdown passes in five consecutive games. If you include rushing touchdowns, he has accounted for at least four touchdowns in each of the last five games.

Peyton Manning is the only player in NFL history with at least four touchdowns in six straight games during his MVP season in 2013 when he set league records with 5,477 passing yards and 55 touchdown passes.

Burrow leads the NFL in passing touchdowns (27), completion percentage (74.7) and ranks second in passing yards (2,795). He is doing that for a Bengals team that leads the AFC North with a 7-2 record.

Gibbs' case for Offensive Player of the Year includes him leading the NFL in rushing yards (1,000), rushing touchdowns (11), yards from scrimmage (1,384) and total touchdowns (13).

At his current pace of 153.8 scrimmage yards per game, Gibbs is on track to break Chris Johnson's single-season record of 2,509 done in 2009.

Smith-Njigba is right on Gibbs' heels because he's on pace for historic levels of receiving production. He has 1,207 receiving yards, 231 more than the No. 2 player in the NFL (CeeDee Lamb: 976).

If you factor in the talent around both players, Smith-Njigba is carrying a heavier burden for the Seattle Seahawks than Gibbs is for the Lions. Gibbs has Jared Goff playing as well as he ever has at quarterback, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams at wide receiver and Sam LaPorta at tight end.

The quarterback situation in Seattle has been all over the place this season. Sam Darnold has struggled with turnovers when healthy. Drew Lock is actually playing really well in his three starts, throwing for 650 yards and six touchdowns.

One reason Lock has been so effective is he's throwing to Smith-Njigba, who has accounted for 51.8 percent of the Seahawks' 2,329 total receiving yards.

Smith-Njigba's 120.7 receiving yards per game has him on pace to be the first receiver to surpass the 2,000-yard mark.

articles.title: Justin Herbert earns an estimated $11 million a year outside football; how the Chargers quarterback built an eight-figure endorsement business alongside his NFL contract
articles.summary: Justin Herbert's biggest paycheque comes from the Los Angeles Chargers, but the quarterback has built another lucrative career away from the field.
articles.body: Justin Herbert's biggest paycheque comes from the Los Angeles Chargers, but the quarterback has built another lucrative career away from the field. His estimated $11 million in annual off-field earnings puts him among the NFL's most commercially successful players. From sportswear and financial services to golf, electronics and trading cards, Herbert has attracted brands across very different markets. The business behind that figure reveals how the Chargers star has turned his football profile into a wider commercial portfolio.Justin Herbert's $11 million off-field earnings put him among NFL's top earnersJustin Herbert's financial success is no longer limited to the money he earns for playing quarterback. Forbes estimated that he collected $71 million in total earnings in 2025, placing him third on its list of the NFL's highest-paid players. The breakdown included $60 million from football and another $11 million from off-field activities.That second figure is particularly interesting. It shows how a player can build a major income stream without taking another snap or signing another contract. However, the $11 million should not be treated as endorsement payments alone. Forbes' off-field estimates include money from endorsements, licensing, appearances and memorabilia, as well as cash returns from certain business interests. The publication bases its estimates on conversations with industry insiders.His playing contract still provides the financial foundation. Herbert signed a five-year, $262.5 million extension with the Chargers in 2023. The agreement briefly made him the highest-paid player in the NFL by average annual value. It included a $45 million option bonus due in 2025, alongside his $15 million salary for that season.The scale of his contract gives brands another reason to take notice. Herbert is not simply a recognisable athlete. He is the face of one of the NFL's most valuable franchises, with a profile that reaches fans well beyond Los Angeles.Nike, SoFi and Callaway Golf form the backbone of Justin Herbert's brand portfolioJustin Herbert's commercial partnerships cover several industries. Forbes lists eight major sponsors: Nike, SoFi, Callaway Golf, TCL, Dr. Squatch, Verizon, Fanatics and Panini. Each offers a different way to connect the quarterback with consumers.Nike has been associated with Herbert since his arrival in the NFL in 2020. The sportswear giant gives him a natural connection to football fans and the wider athletic market. His partnership with SoFi, however, stands out because it included something beyond a traditional advertising arrangement.In September 2022, SoFi announced a three-year partnership with Herbert. The agreement also gave him an equity stake in the financial services company. He appeared in its advertising campaign, which encouraged customers to move away from unsatisfactory banking services.Herbert welcomed the opportunity, explaining why the partnership felt like a natural fit.“Given our shared values and the fact that I am already a SoFi member, I’m thrilled to partner with SoFi in an official capacity to help guide myself and others to financial success,” said Herbert. “In order to set myself up for success – both on and off the field – it’s critical to build and maintain great relationships, especially when it comes to my finances. It’s great to have found a partner in SoFi and I look forward to all that’s to come.”The equity element makes the deal especially notable. Instead of receiving only a conventional endorsement payment, Herbert also received a stake in the business. The value of that stake has not been publicly disclosed, so its contribution to his earnings cannot be calculated from available information.Justin Herbert turns his love of golf into another business opportunityOne of Justin Herbert's most natural brand connections comes away from the football field. The Chargers quarterback is an avid golfer, and Callaway Golf turned that personal interest into a commercial partnership in April 2023.The multi-year agreement made Herbert a Callaway ambassador. He would use the company's equipment, appear in branded content and support initiatives aimed at introducing more young people to golf. The partnership also suited his interest in the sport, rather than placing him in an unrelated advertising role.Herbert has spoken about why the relationship appealed to him.“Golf is a sport that’s all about precision and that’s something that resonates with me as a quarterback,” Herbert said. “That’s why I’m thrilled to team up with Callaway, a brand that understands the importance of attention to detail and the value of hard work. Whether I’m playing a round with friends or playing for my annual golf invitational, I know I can count on Callaway to provide me with the gear and support I need to succeed.”His connection to golf also extends into charity work. Herbert has hosted an annual golf invitational in his hometown of Eugene, Oregon, to benefit Kidsports, a nonprofit that supports youth sports. The partnership therefore gives Callaway a chance to reach football fans while connecting with a wider audience interested in golf and youth development.It is a useful example of how an athlete's genuine interests can create commercial opportunities. A brand partnership becomes more convincing when the product fits the person's life.TCL, Dr. Squatch, Verizon and Fanatics expand Herbert's commercial reachJustin Herbert's remaining partnerships show how far his appeal extends beyond sports equipment and financial services.TCL named him its North American NFL brand ambassador in February 2023. The electronics company planned to feature him in advertising across its product categories and use his social media presence for marketing campaigns. Herbert also appeared in promotional material highlighting the company's televisions and smartphones.“I am really excited to partner with TCL,” said Herbert. “I’m very impressed with the performance of their products and excited that the fans are able to have an immersive experience on game day, whether they’re watching us play on a big screen at home or watching us on their phone.”His work with Dr. Squatch takes him into the men's grooming market. The brand has featured him in campaigns promoting its personal care products, giving it access to a sports audience through a familiar NFL face.Verizon adds a telecommunications company to the portfolio, while Fanatics and Panini connect Herbert with merchandise, collectibles and trading cards. These partnerships allow his commercial profile to reach fans who may follow his career through products and memorabilia as much as through live games.Herbert has also appeared in Subway advertising and previously worked with Kendall Auto Group, a dealership network with roots in his hometown. Those appearances add to a business portfolio that has developed over several seasons.The financial details of most individual deals remain private. There is no public breakdown showing exactly how much each company pays him, and the Forbes sponsor list does not confirm that every partnership remains active in November 2026.Still, the wider picture is clear. Herbert's estimated $11 million in off-field earnings reflects a business strategy built around different audiences and interests. His Chargers contract provides the sporting foundation, but his brand relationships have created a second source of income that stands on its own. For the quarterback, success is paying off in more ways than one.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A.J. Brown’s Patriots trade disaster could cost him his 2027 NFL season after injury plagued 2026 campaign
articles.summary: All that for what? A.J. Brown was unhappy with the Philadelphia Eagles because his Jalen Hurts targets were split with DeVonta Smith.
articles.body: All that for what? A.J. Brown was unhappy with the Philadelphia Eagles because his Jalen Hurts targets were split with DeVonta Smith.He reportedly started his own trade rumors ahead of the 2026 offseason and season. The rumors reached then-The Athletic’s NFL reporter Dianna Russini. She was reportedly in touch with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel in the 2025 season and 2026 offseason.The Patriots wanted a powerful wide receiver for their ace quarterback Drake Maye. The coach may have suggested Philadelphia Eagles WR A.J. Brown. Brown got traded to the Patriots.10 games into the 2026 NFL season, A.J. Brown could record only 11 receptions on 26 targets for 128 receiving yards, zero touchdowns, and one fumble across four games. He suffered three injuries in his 2026 campaign. All that for what?A.J. Brown could lose his 2027 NFL season with Patriots for this reasonOn Sept. 9, 2026, A.J. Brown suffered a grade 3 right ankle injury when he went down on a third-down incomplete pass from Drake Maye. Brown was seen in a walking boot. He was placed on short-term injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. He missed four games.On Oct. 28, 2026, he suffered a grade 1 knee strain ahead of the Week 8 game. He was listed as questionable for the game after a degenerative knee injury flared up in practice. He was still slowed by the ankle injury he suffered in September. After missing two games [Weeks 8, 9] due to a degenerative knee injury, he returned for Week 10 vs. the Detroit Lions.On Nov. 15, he suffered a hamstring injury in the third quarter of New England’s Week 10 loss to Detroit in Germany. He went to the locker room but was ruled out for the rest of the game.Week 11 is the Patriots’ bye week, which will allow him to recover. However, speculation about his 2026 offseason trade from the Philadelphia Eagles has now become a big topic of discussion - so much so that CBS Sports HQ analyst and former Tennessee Titans general manager Ran Carthon urged New England to cut A.J. Brown before the 2027 NFL season.There is a potential out in Brown’s contract after the 2026 NFL season, according to one CBS Sports analyst discussing the trade. So, when Carthon was asked about the Patriots potentially letting go of Brown, he said they “have to.”“You have to. You have to cut your losses and be willing to say, ‘Guys, we were wrong. This was just not a good sound decision by us,’” Carthon said. “You don’t want to compound a mistake by holding onto it too long, trying to prove to someone else that you were right.You cut your losses because here’s the thing - you don’t want to have, especially as a young New England Patriots team, and this is not even an A.J. Brown thing; this is just, to me, a macrovision look at it - you don’t want to have anyone that’s going to come in and disrupt your culture, especially as you’re trying to establish a new culture.And if that person, whoever you bring in, is doing that, and I’m not saying he is, you’ve got to cut your ties.”When the whole world is probably contemplating his New England departure, good news comes to him through his wife, Kelsey Nicole Riley Brown.A.J. Brown’s wife Kelsey Nicole Riley Brown is officially a licensed registered nurseA.J. Brown’s wife, Kelsey Nicole Riley Brown, shared five snapshots of her nursing life, right from her childhood dream to her graduation on Instagram. She officially earned her [registered nurse] RN license a few days back. She captioned the Instagram post: “By the GRACE OF GOD, guess who’s officially a licensed RN 🥹🤍For those who don’t know, I started nursing school back in the beginning 2021. I did one yr of nursing school in Houston. I got pregnant end of 2021 and decided to move to Tennessee beginning of 2022 where I transferred to go to school there and was supposed to continue Sept 2024.That didn’t happen because we moved to Philly… I decided to just sit down for a couple years lol. I started back nursing school again in 2024 while juggling being a mom, friend, supporting partner, and everything else that comes with those titles.2 years later November 18, 2026 I can finally say it all paid off . All the anxiety, stress, missed trips, late nights and early mornings, flying back and forth plus moving again, were worth it . And the HUGEST THANK YOU to all my family and friends who pushed me, held me accountable and supported me. I LOVE YALL the most 🤍🤍.”Congratulations poured in from all over the NFL, including Drake Maye’s wife, Ann Michael Maye - “So awesome!!!! Congrats ❤️” and Dianna Russini wrote, “Congratulations. All the best!” Russini may be trying to cheer A.J. Brown up. Anyhow, if he’s cut from the New England Patriots, where will he end up? Back with the Philadelphia Eagles? Or somewhere else. Only time will tell.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' Philadelphia return brings back familiar memories as Steelers veteran addresses the city's intimidating fan culture
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has faced the Philadelphia Eagles several times during his NFL career, but his next visit to Lincoln Financial Field comes with a different
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has faced the Philadelphia Eagles several times during his NFL career, but his next visit to Lincoln Financial Field comes with a different story. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback will return to a city known for making life uncomfortable for visiting teams, carrying memories of both victories and difficult afternoons. Ahead of Sunday's November 22 meeting, Rodgers spoke openly about Philadelphia's passionate supporters. Rather than dismissing their reputation, the veteran quarterback showed respect for the atmosphere, admitting that his previous experiences with Eagles fans have been memorable.Aaron Rodgers opens up about Philadelphia's intimidating fan baseRodgers knows that playing in Philadelphia is rarely a quiet experience. The Eagles faithful have built a reputation for being loud, demanding and fiercely loyal, and opposing quarterbacks often feel that pressure from the opening kickoff.Yet the 42-year-old does not appear bothered by what awaits him. Speaking to reporters ahead of the Steelers' visit, Rodgers offered a surprisingly warm assessment of the city and its sports culture.“It’s a good fan base, you know. Really good sports town,” Rodgers told reporters.“Got some great teams, some historic teams there, you know, in hockey, baseball, and basketball. Obviously, the football has had a lot of success over the years too. It’s a rowdy group. I mean, I’ve had some interesting interactions over the years there, but it’s a fun place to play.”The comment about interesting interactions is worth noting. Philadelphia supporters are known for making their feelings clear, whether their team is winning or struggling. Rodgers has experienced that intensity firsthand, but he does not seem to hold any grudges.His response also reflects an appreciation for the city's wider sporting identity. Philadelphia fans do not limit their passion to football. Their connection with the Eagles, Phillies, Flyers and 76ers makes the city a difficult place for visiting athletes, regardless of the sport.Rodgers' previous meetings with the Eagles add another layer to Sunday's gameThis will be Rodgers' fifth appearance in Philadelphia, but his first wearing a Steelers uniform. His previous four visits all came during his time with the Green Bay Packers, and the results were evenly split.Rodgers lost his first trip in 2006 before leading Green Bay to a victory in 2010. He returned in 2016 and picked up another win, only to suffer a defeat against Philadelphia in November 2022. Across seven career meetings with the Eagles, he holds a 4-3 record.That history gives Sunday's matchup an added personal angle. Rodgers knows the stadium, understands the crowd and has experienced both sides of the result. This time, however, he will have a different team around him and a new challenge to handle.The Steelers enter the contest at 6-3 after losing 38-18 to the Cincinnati Bengals in their previous game. Rodgers has completed 59.9% of his passes for 2,014 yards, 15 touchdowns and six interceptions through nine appearances. Those numbers show that Pittsburgh has received steady production from its veteran quarterback, although the latest defeat exposed problems the team needs to address.Philadelphia, meanwhile, sits at 2-7 and has not won a game since September. The Eagles will be eager to use their home crowd to make life difficult for Pittsburgh, especially as they look to find some direction after a disappointing run.For Rodgers, the timing of this return makes it an interesting test. He has handled Philadelphia before, but past results offer little protection against a team desperate to respond in front of its supporters. The Steelers need a strong performance after their loss to Cincinnati, and Rodgers will have to manage both the Eagles' defense and the noise around him.His comments suggest he enjoys that part of the game. He respects the fans, remembers the atmosphere and seems to understand why Philadelphia remains such a difficult road destination. On Sunday, he will find out whether his latest visit brings another winning memory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Kylie Kelce is usually pretty open when it comes to sharing glimpses of her life with Jason Kelce, but one fan may have taken that curiosity a little too far. The podcast host recently found herself facing a rather awkward question about what goes on behind closed bedroom doors with her NFL star husband, and her reaction was priceless.Kylie Kelce has hilarious reaction to awkward question about her and Jason Kelce’s bedroom lifeDuring the November 19 episode of her podcast, Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce, Kylie came across a fan question that left her visibly unimpressed. The person asked, "Jason is strong, muscular, with football and kids. How would you spice up the bedroom?"Kylie did not even try to hide her reaction. She let out an audible groan before making it clear that the question was a little too personal."Yes, that audible groan is the appropriate response. What the actual f***?" she said.But Kylie wasn't done there. She also explained that this was exactly why she had changed the name of her podcast's question-and-answer segment from "Ask Me Anything" to "Ask Me Some Things.""It's because this is the ridiculous s*** that ends up in our inbox," she explained.And while she could have simply skipped the question, Kylie decided to have a little fun with it. Offering a sarcastic response, she suggested that the couple could "put some cinnamon sticks" in the bedroom. She then made it clear that she understood the fan was probably not asking about actual spices.The exchange quickly turned into one of those amusing podcast moments that fans can expect from Kylie, who has never been particularly shy about speaking her mind.Kylie Kelce isn't afraid to keep fans in checkKylie and Jason have been married since 2018 and share four daughters. While Jason's NFL career and their family life have often put them in the spotlight, Kylie has also built a following of her own through her podcast and candid conversations.However, this latest exchange showed that being open with fans does not mean every part of their marriage is up for discussion. And judging by her reaction, Kylie has a pretty clear idea of where to draw that line.Her cinnamon-stick comeback may not have been the bedroom advice the fan was looking for, but it certainly made for an entertaining podcast moment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Joe Burrow and Olivia Ponton are once again at the center of relationship speculation, and this time, cheating rumors have added a fresh twist to their already closely watched romance. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback and the model have kept their personal lives largely private, but a mysterious blind item and Olivia's latest social media activity have left fans wondering whether everything is well between the two.An NFL cheating blind item, a cryptic TikTok and Joe Burrow: What's happening with Olivia Ponton?The latest conversation began after an anonymous gossip post started circulating online. Published by Crazy Days and Nights on November 15, Blind Item #11 described an unnamed A-list NFL quarterback who allegedly cheated on his model girlfriend. The post also claimed that the woman later cheated on him in retaliation and sent him a recording of the encounter.Adding to the curiosity, Ponton has recently been sharing glimpses of her vacation in Guatemala, where she has been documenting a challenging hiking adventure.The model described completing a 24-hour hiking experience as life-changing, sharing updates about the physical challenge, altitude sickness and the exhaustion that followed. She also posted several videos that caught people's attention, including one carrying the caption "Happiest ever."The timing of her posts has fueled further discussion, with some social media users interpreting her content through the lens of the ongoing relationship rumors. However, Ponton has not directly connected her Guatemala getaway or her TikTok videos to Burrow or the cheating allegations.The anonymous post did not identify the quarterback or his girlfriend, so social media users began connecting the description to Burrow and Ponton. One fan even reacted to the speculation by writing, "Joe Burrow getting played wasn't on my bingo card this year."However, there is no verified evidence that Burrow is the quarterback described in the blind item, or that either he or Ponton has been involved in infidelity. The allegations remain unsubstantiated gossip rather than confirmed details about their relationship.Olivia Ponton's past cheating confession adds another layerInterestingly, the rumors have also brought attention back to something Ponton previously shared about her dating history.During an appearance on her Booked & Busy podcast, the model revealed that she had been cheated on in every one of her previous relationships."I have been cheated on in all of my past relationships. Literally every single one of them. All of them," she said.Ponton also explained that she views cheating as a reflection of the person being unfaithful rather than the person being betrayed. While her comments were about her past experiences, they have resurfaced as fans discuss the latest allegations involving Burrow. She did not accuse Burrow of cheating or suggest that her comments were connected to their rumored relationship.Where do Joe Burrow and Olivia Ponton stand?Burrow and Ponton have been romantically linked since December 2024, when the model was at the quarterback's Ohio home during a reported burglary. Their connection has continued to attract attention through public appearances and sightings together.They were spotted together at the 2025 Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix, and their appearances at several events throughout 2026 kept the dating speculation alive. Ponton was also spotted at Bengals training camp in August, where she was seen spending time talking with Burrow.Neither has publicly confirmed the exact status of their relationship. articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Drops Cryptic Quote on DC Christian Parker After Change in Play-Caller
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones commented Friday on the notion that he has not spoken to defensive coordinator Christian Parker since stripping him of his play-calling duties this week.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones commented Friday on the notion that he has not spoken to defensive coordinator Christian Parker since stripping him of his play-calling duties this week.

During an appearance on 105.3 The Fan (h/t Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News ), Jones was asked about not speaking with Parker in the wake of the move, and he responded by saying, "I don't have an issue and I don't think anybody else should if they know what I know."

The subject came up after Parker told reporters Thursday that he had not spoken with Jones after the move was made.

On Wednesday, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters that while Parker would stay on as DC, senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine was taking over defensive play-calling duties for the remainder of the season.

On Thursday, Parker spoke publicly for the first time since being stripped of play-calling duties, and he admitted to reporters that he considered leaving the team before ultimately deciding to stick it out.

"Initially in your mind, you're thinking about all the things, and in my opinion, that would've been running from it," Parker said. "At the end of the day, I've got a job to do, and my job is to be the defensive coordinator of the Dallas Cowboys. Whether that is calling plays on Sunday, obviously that's not the case anymore, but on Monday, on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and whatever day we play, there is a focus level that I need to have. There's a contribution that I still have to be able to maintain. That is regardless of feelings and anything else. And I think that our focus is aligned in the building, No. 1, with me and [Pettine], [and] No. 2, with the staff and with the players."

After serving as the Philadelphia Eagles' passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach from 2024 through 2025, Parker was hired this past offseason as the Cowboys' new defensive coordinator, replacing Matt Eberflus.

Entering the 2026 campaign, Dallas had ranked 28th in total defense and 31st in scoring defense in 2024, and 30th in total defense and 32nd in scoring defense in 2025.

Things have not gotten any better under Parker in 2026, as the Cowboys are 32nd in total defense and 30th in scoring defense, contributing heavily to a disappointing 4-6 start.

The final straw for Parker came this past Sunday when Dallas' defense allowed 584 total yards in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Dallas still has a chance to contend for a playoff spot in the weak NFC East, as the division-leading New York Giants are only 5-3-1.

The defense has to get better in order for the Cowboys to stay in the race, and taking play-calling responsibilities away from Parker was a major decision meant to do just that.

articles.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua potentially out for the rest of the 2026 season after undergoing MCL surgery
articles.summary: Nacua has been on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent surgery to repair his right MCL this week, head coach Sean McVay announced on Friday . The procedure will rule him out for the next few months, which could result in him missing the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

"We always thought [it] was a possibility," McVay said regarding Nacua's surgery. "It's going to be a couple months and we're going to have to go on without him."

The 6-4 Rams are currently tied for second in the NFC West and have seven more games left in the regular season. McVay did not have a definitive timeline for a return. The team is currently scheduled to play its Week 18 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Jan. 3, a game that could be flexed depending on what the playoff picture looks like at the time.

McVay did not rule out a Nacua return should the Rams make the postseason, but said, "you're planning on not having him."

Nacua, who missed two games early in the season with a hip injury, was ruled out for Week 10 after being placed on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries. On Thursday, the NFL announced he was being suspended three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy.

The IR stint and suspension will run concurrently with the ban costing the wide receiver $950,000 in salary.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the NFL did not know Nacua had the surgery on Tuesday when the suspension was handed down.

Through seven games, Nacua, who is in the final year of his contract, has recorded 715 receiving yards on 70 receptions with four touchdowns.

articles.title: Tom Brady reveals the biggest challenge of his $375 million FOX career as he opens up about his new reality
articles.summary: Tom Brady has spent years meeting the highest expectations in professional football.
articles.body: Tom Brady has spent years meeting the highest expectations in professional football. But his second career at FOX Sports has brought a different kind of pressure, one that even seven Super Bowl titles could not prepare him for. The former New England Patriots quarterback is now in his second season as the network's lead NFL analyst, and he knows the responsibility goes well beyond breaking down plays. Speaking with NHL legend Tie Domi, Brady opened up about the challenge of living up to FOX's $375 million investment while making sure the people watching at home get something worthwhile every Sunday.Tom Brady feels the pressure to deliver on his $375 million FOX dealBrady's 10-year, $375 million agreement with FOX Sports, signed in 2022, made him the highest-paid broadcaster in sports. However, the money has not made him any less conscious of what the network expects from him.During an appearance on Tie Domi's DAZN interview series, "Keeping It Real with Tie," Brady explained that he still considers himself a student of broadcasting. His NFL experience gives him a strong understanding of the game, but communicating that knowledge to a live audience is a different skill.“I think what I do is I feel a responsibility to do a good job for people,” Brady said. “So I have a lot to learn still. It’s only my second year, but a few things I really love about it.”That admission says plenty about how Brady views his new profession. He is not treating his playing record as proof that he should automatically succeed behind a microphone. Instead, he wants to keep improving.He also made it clear that his performance is not an individual effort. Brady praised play-by-play partner Kevin Burkhardt, along with sideline reporters Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi and the production crew working behind the scenes.“I love the team aspect. Like Kevin Burkhardt’s my partner. I love KB. He’s great,” Brady added.For someone who spent 23 seasons relying on teammates, the importance of that connection is hardly surprising. He sees the FOX crew as a family, and he understands that a strong broadcast depends on everyone doing their part.Tom Brady wants to reward the fans and avoid letting FOX downBrady's biggest motivation, however, appears to come from the people watching at home. He understands that fans give up part of their weekends to follow the NFL, and he wants their time to feel worthwhile.“They commit to you. It’s like, why don’t you go out there and do something for them?” Brady said.He compared that responsibility to watching films featuring Tom Hanks, Tom Cruise and Denzel Washington. The goal, in his view, is to give people an experience they enjoy.That thinking also explains why he remains concerned about meeting FOX's expectations. Brady does not want his contract or reputation to become a substitute for delivering quality work.“I feel like that’s how I want to be as a broadcaster, too. Like, they committed to me. FOX, first of all, they committed to me. I don’t want to let the executives down at FOX who committed to me. I don’t want to let my teammates down, and I don’t want to let the broadcast down. Like, I gotta go deliver,” Brady said.His early broadcasts attracted criticism, particularly over his delivery and ability to translate his football knowledge into clear analysis. The improvement since his 2024 debut has been noticeable.Brady still has plenty to learn, but his comments suggest he understands what the job demands. For him, the real measure of that $375 million opportunity is not the contract itself. It is whether viewers, colleagues and the network can count on him every Sunday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Daniel Jones' Release Impacts Colts' Salary Cap After Signing Historic $88M Contract
articles.summary: Eight months after giving Daniel Jones a historic two-year contract in free agency, the Indianapolis Colts are looking at a significant dead-cap charge in 2027 with him no longer on the roster.
articles.body:
Eight months after giving Daniel Jones a historic two-year contract in free agency, the Indianapolis Colts are looking at a significant dead-cap charge in 2027 with him no longer on the roster.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced on Friday that Jones has been released following their 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans.

The move means Jones will have to clear waivers before becoming a free agent. Assuming no team enters a claim, the Colts are facing a $35.2 million dead cap hit next season from his two-year, $88 million deal.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, if a team were to put in a waiver claim on Jones, it would be assumed they are taking on his $10.5 million injury guarantee for next season.

Jones' dead-cap charge puts him on a list with Aaron Rodgers as the only players in NFL history to have multiple dead-cap hits of at least $35 million. The New York Giants took a $47.1 million charge when they released him late in the 2024 season after signing him to a four-year, $160 million extension in March 2023.

It's been obvious for some time the Colts put themselves in a disastrous position. Their difficulties started last season by trading two first-round picks to the New York Jets for Sauce Gardner.

Even though the Colts were 7-2 at the time of the trade and had an explosive offense, that's a lot of draft capital to give up for a non-quarterback.

Jones tore his Achilles one month after the trade, ending his season and leaving his future uncertain. The Colts finished 2025 on a seven-game losing streak to end up 8-9 and miss the playoffs.

Indianapolis showed no real concern about Jones' ability to rebound by signing him to a two-year contract in free agency. The team also gave Alec Pierce a four-year, $116 million deal.

Pierce played in two games before going on injured reserve with a heel injury after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. There is currently no indication he is going to return this season.

Jones was able to start the season coming off his Achilles injury, but the results left plenty to be desired. He threw for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and an NFL-high 13 interceptions in 11 starts.

The upside for the Colts is their cap is in good standing even with Jones' charge factored in. They project to have $89.5 million available in the offseason to add to their roster.

Unfortunately, the money comes at a time when the Colts don't have an obvious starting quarterback on the roster and no first-round pick. Based on the current standings , they will be sending the No. 6 overall selection in the 2027 draft to the Jets.

The list of potential free-agent quarterbacks going into the offseason includes Kirk Cousins, Deshaun Watson, Geno Smith, Kyler Murray, Jacoby Brissett, Gardner Minshew and Carson Wentz. The latter three in that group have had a previous stint with the Colts.

Jones has made $172.7 million in his eight-year NFL career. He has made 94 appearances (93 starts) during that period, racking up 19,657 passing yards, 96 touchdowns and 68 interceptions.

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Top NFL Landing Spots After Stunning Colts Release
articles.summary: Teams still in need of a quarterback after the trade deadline just got a surprising opportunity to snag one.
articles.body:
Teams still in need of a quarterback after the trade deadline just got a surprising opportunity to snag one.

The Indianapolis Colts announced Friday the team had released Daniel Jones after a 3-8 start to the season.

Any team that claims Jones off waivers would owe him $2.345 million ($2.1 million guaranteed) over the remainder of the season, per Spotrac . His $38 million salary for 2027 is non-guaranteed, Spotrac noted.

Jones has completed a career-low 58.4 percent of his passes and leads the NFL with 13 interceptions, but his experience and relatively low salary cap impact could encourage another team to offer him a chance to bounce back down the stretch.

The Minnesota Vikings, New England Patriots, Philadelphia Eagles and Baltimore Ravens could all be potential landing spots for Jones after injuries tested each team's quarterback depth early this season.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the Colts turned down trade interest regarding Jones from the Vikings ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

The Vikings (7-2) turned instead to the Las Vegas Raiders to acquire veteran signal caller Kirk Cousins, who led his new team to victory over the Green Bay Packers in his return to the franchise last Sunday.

Jones, like Cousins, has history with the Vikings, with which he finished out the 2024 season following his release by the New York Giants.

He didn't see any action in Minnesota but later expressed admiration of the Vikings coaching staff after signing with the Colts the following offseason.

The Vikings could now consider reuniting with Jones as insurance behind Cousins as the team looks to capitalize on their elite defense by gearing up for a playoff run.

The Patriots (5-5) are in need of a quarterback after Drake Maye suffered a fractured right fibula last Sunday that ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter reported "won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season."

There is a "possibility, but hardly a certainty, that Maye could return toward the end of the season if New England is in playoff contention," Reiss and Schefter reported.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer noted Jones' experience with former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who like Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels is a graduate of the Nick Saban coaching tree, "could make him a fit" in the New England offense.

Tommy DeVito is currently set to start with Behren Morton as backup for as long as Maye is out. The Patriots could look to target Jones if they feel the quarterback could give New England a better shot at extending their season long enough for Maye to return.

The Eagles (2-7) have been missing Jalen Hurts since Oct. 11 following the quarterback's diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis.

Philadelphia went on to lose three straight games with Tanner McKee before turning to Joe Milton ahead of last week's bye.

Head coach Nick Sirianni said earlier this week Milton will return as starter, while first-year OC Sean Mannion will continue calling plays despite the Eagles' offensive struggles early this season.

Jones has experience with Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley after spending five seasons together in New York.

The Eagles could hope adding a veteran quarterback who is used to playing with Barkley could help speed up Mannion's adjustment down the stretch of the season.

The Ravens (4-6) were another team that expressed interest in trading for Jones ahead of the deadline, per Schefter .

After the Colts decided to hang on to Jones, the Ravens acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals instead.

Brissett struggled early in his Monday Ravens debut, ultimately throwing for 340 yards with an interception as Baltimore allowed the Los Angeles Chargers to claim their first win of the season.

The Ravens could consider adding another experienced quarterback in order to better set up star running back Derrick Henry to keep this offense afloat down the stretch.

articles.title: Patriots QB Drake Maye reportedly has fractured right fibula, could return later this season
articles.summary: Drake Maye injured his ankle after being sacked on the team's first drive in Week 10.
articles.body:
Following testing, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula in Week 10, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss .

Maye will not require surgery and there is a small chance he could be back for the Patriots late in the regular season if they are contending for an AFC playoff spot.

Maye sustained the injury during the team's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. It happened on the team's first drive, which ended after Maye was sacked by Lions star Aidan Hutchinson.

Maye's injury actually wasn't the focus initially. Following the sack, Hutchinson sustained a torn ACL while celebrating the play. He'll miss the rest of the season due to the injury.

The true extent of Maye's injury came to light on the Patriots' next offensive drive. Backup Tommy DeVito entered the game in place of Maye, who was spotted on the broadcast walking back to the team's locker room. Maye was unable to return to the game, and the team was tight-lipped about the nature of the injury.

Later Sunday, reports started to emerge suggesting Maye could miss "a while." Those reports received more clarity Monday, when it was revealed Maye remained in Germany to receive further evaluation. By Monday morning, it was reported the Patriots feared Maye was dealing with a " significant lower leg injury ," possibly a fracture.

The injury could end Maye's third NFL season prematurely. While the 24-year-old got off to a tough start, turning the ball over seven times in the team's first three games, he proved last year's excellence was not a fluke. In the six games leading up to Week 10, Maye had 17 passing touchdowns against five interceptions. He was on pace for yet another strong year before the injury.

While Maye's long-term outlook remains strong, the Patriots' short-term outlook appears disastrous. Following the team's loss in Week 10, the Patriots sit at 5-5 through 10 games. The playoffs are still very much in the picture, but only if the team can rally around its new quarterback. That didn't happen in Week 10, as the team looked listless with DeVito under center.

But DeVito will have the bye week to get fully up to speed. When the Patriots return to action, they'll take on the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers, giving DeVito an opportunity for a big game in his first start.

After that, though, things get much harder for the Patriots. During the last six weeks of the regular season, New England will take on the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos. The team very likely needs to win at least two, possibly three of those games to secure a spot in the postseason.

Getting that done without Maye will be extremely difficult.

Steichen did not give an expansive reason for releasing Jones but the guarantee, which would have put the Colts on the hook for 2027 if Jones got hurt, was likely involved in the logic. And that was too high a financial risk for a quarterback that has been a massive disappointment in Indianapolis after he was a massive disappointment with the New York Giants. Jones makes more sense on a team desperate for middling quarterback help after he clears waivers. The New England Patriots, who are managing a Drake Maye leg injury, make sense. The Colts pretty much waved the white flag on the 2026 season at the NFL trade deadline nearly two weeks ago. They sent multiple players off in return for modest 2027 draft choice compensation. This move is not that. This move feels more like the club simply ridding itself of a potential injury cost for next season while also moving on from a player who frustrated people within the organization this season. SHANE STEICHEN SAYS DANIEL JONES WON'T BE BENCHED BUT COACH AND GENERAL MANAGER CHRIS BALLARD ARE IN TROUBLE That frustration came because Jones played well for Indy early in the 2025 season before getting hurt. The Colts believed that was the real Jones and rewarded him last offseason with a two-year contract worth $88 million. Then Jones didn't live up to the salary. He leads the NFL with 13 interceptions. He's thrown an interception in six consecutive games. And he always has the look of a victim on his face. MORE PROOF THAT ANY TEAM TRADING FOR DANIEL JONES AT THE NFL TRADE DEADLINE IS CHASING FOOL'S GOLD Jones is not a victim. He pocketed $50 million from the Colts this season to start 11 games. And the Colts might've known this was possible because Jones got paid by the New York Giants in 2023 when they gave him a four-year deal worth $160 million... ...And then his play fell off the table once he got paid and had his contract terminated in 2024. So now the Colts turn to Richardson, their once and future starter. He was drafted with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 draft. The team picked him knowing he needed to develop after playing only one full season at the University of Florida. Except he never developed because he was injured multiple times, taking him out of the lineup. And then he struggled, which also got him benched. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So the guy needing experience didn't get experience. That led Richardson to request a trade earlier this season. Now he instead gets the final six games of the season to prove whatever he can prove. "It's going to be great," Steichen said. "He's going to get a full week of practice. From his rookie year to now obviously he's matured a lot with his preparation and how he goes about it. "And so to get him a full week of practice going into the game, I think is benefit him well." articles.title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley Reacts to Daniel Jones' Surprise Release by Colts, 'It Sucks'
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was asked on Friday about the Indianapolis Colts releasing quarterback Daniel Jones.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was asked on Friday about the Indianapolis Colts releasing quarterback Daniel Jones.

"It sucks," Barkley said. "Obviously, their season ... wasn't going as well, and they had a rough night last night, too. That's part of the business. But, you know, it's adversity. It's not the first time [Jones] is going to face adversity. And I know him really well, one of my best friends, and I know whenever his next opportunity comes, he's going to work his butt off and be ready for it."

The Colts announced they were releasing the veteran quarterback after their 26-3 loss against the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football.

Jones signed with the Colts last season and led them to a promising 8-2 start before injuries derailed his campaign. Indianapolis finished the season with seven consecutive losses, and the Colts have now lost 15 of their last 18 regular-season games dating back to last season.

In his 11 games with the Colts this season, Jones had just 1,974 passing yards with seven touchdowns and a league-high 13 interceptions. He has also had his worst season as a runner with a career-low 8.9 rushing yards per game.

The 29-year-old quarterback was benched in favor of backup Anthony Richardson after completing just 12 of his 27 pass attempts with one interception against Houston on Thursday night.

Barkley and Jones began their careers with the New York Giants, and they developed a bond while sharing the backfield for five seasons. Barkley, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, was named AP NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year after a stellar debut season, and Jones was drafted the following year with the No. 6 overall pick.

Barkley and Jones led the Giants to a playoff appearance in 2022 and pulled off a 31-24 upset over the Minnesota Vikings in the wild card round.

They were seen as promising talents who would lead the franchise to success for years to come, but those plans fell apart after Barkley's messy departure in free agency after the 2023 season. Jones struggled without Barkley, and he was released during the 2024 season after starting just 10 games.

articles.title: Now what? Colts should have traded Daniel Jones when they had the chance
articles.summary: This move was nothing short of a stunner, if only from a financial standpoint. From a football standpoint, the Colts couldn't justify keeping Jones as QB1? C...
articles.body:
Here's the Daniel Jones timeline for the past eight months — and stick with us, because it's a wild ride.

The Colts signed Jones to the largest two-year contract in NFL history despite coming off Achilles surgery a few months earlier.

The Colts kept Jones as their starter, without any new competition, this season.

The Colts continued to put Jones as QB1 while he struggled, throwing interceptions in 10 of his 11 starts.

The Colts reportedly listened to trade offers for their starting QB prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline before ultimately passing.

Whew . Caught up? Good. Now consider: Cutting Jones will cost the team nearly $15 million in dead salary-cap money, plus another $35 million for next year.

Friday's move was nothing short of a stunner, if only from a financial standpoint. From a football standpoint, the Colts couldn't justify keeping him as the starter? Cutting him now, knowing what a hit they'd take? It almost feels personal at this point.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen clearly had enough of him Thursday night. The speculation on why Steichen hadn't gone to Anthony Richardson Sr. sooner was that the coach might have trusted Richardson even less .

Steichen might also be in self-preservation mode, trying to hold together a ship that was partially stripped before the trade deadline and already in rough shape before that. But assuming Steichen didn't reach his breaking point during Thursday's game, why did the Colts wait to get rid of him?

And not only for nothing. It actually cost the Colts money and flexibility to release him now. It doesn't get much uglier than that.

Why didn't the Colts trade Daniel Jones?

There have been credible reports that multiple teams inquired about Jones' availability before the trade deadline, including the Ravens and Vikings. Others might also have checked in on him. The Colts held firm. The Ravens got Jacoby Brissett and the Vikings landed Kirk Cousins.

This feels like a major missed opportunity. By releasing Jones, the Colts got nothing and made their situation worse. Even with the potential return of a Day 3 draft pick and a slightly better impact on their salary cap, the Colts passed.

It should be noted that the Vikings feel great about Cousins, and it's possible that their interest in Jones was more of a fallback option. The Ravens? Brissett's numbers over the past two seasons have been slightly better, so it's fair to say that they might have preferred the QB they ended up with.

But any potential interest in Jones should have been met with a take-him-off-our-hands type of offer — the kind a team couldn't turn down. Someone is going to sign him here in the coming days, and given all the QB injuries around the league this season, it wouldn't be a stunner to see Jones start a game at some point this season.

The Colts were more than willing to part with other assets prior to the deadline, including DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and Josh Downs. They listened to offers for Jones and Jonathan Taylor but ended up keeping both. Taylor had 11 carries for 21 yards and four catches for 6 yards on Thursday. Jones struggled and was cut. Little of this makes sense.

When general manager Chris Ballard was fired midseason and replaced by interim GM Ed Dodds, it felt like an opportunity for Dodds to earn the full-time job by starting the process of replenishing the Colts' draft pool. They've done that, but they've also thrown away large chunks of meat still on the bone.

Dodds was dealt a tough hand (one he helped put together, for what it's worth), but it's arguable he has played it poorly — unless Jones' release was mandated from on high. That's possible. If it's true, the Colts' situation is even uglier than it appears.

The Colts still need a quarterback, and finding a decent one won't be easy

Since Andrew Luck's shocking retirement in August 2019, the Colts have started 12 different quarterbacks. Jones' 24 starts were the most from that group in that span, but it's highly likely some new names are added to the list next season. This franchise is starting to become synonymous with QB instability, and after two decades of having Peyton Manning and Luck, that's a bitter pill to swallow.

The remaining options on the roster this season are Richardson and Riley Leonard. The Colts don't appear to have great belief in either one. They declined the fifth-year option on Richardson's rookie deal, making him a free agent this spring, and have been reluctant to give him much of a shot prior to now. Leonard was last seen in last year's Week 18 start and hasn't played a snap in 2026.

The assumption is that Richardson will play elsewhere next season. He certainly has a chance to rewrite his story in Indy as Jones' replacement , but whatever he does down the stretch will likely serve as an audition for his next stop. Leonard could be back in 2027, but it's unlikely he'd be anything higher than a backup to start next season.

The Colts could have waited until the offseason and made Jones a post-June 1 cut, with far less of a salary cap footprint. The question of whether to keep Jones is settled, but the problems are only starting.

The Sauce Gardner trade cost them next year's first-round draft pick, and though the pre-deadline trades netted them some Day 2 and 3 ammunition over the next two years, it still makes acquiring a quarterback tougher come springtime.

The Colts can still move into the bottom of Round 1 for a quarterback in next spring's draft. But will there be a viable starting candidate available in that range? What was thought to be a banner QB crop in the 2027 NFL Draft is turning into more of a grab-bag situation, depending on which underclassmen declare.

Perhaps an unexpected veteran or two could hit the market. The veteran route feels more likely now, at least from an immediate-starter perspective. But will there be starting-quality options? That hope feels dubious now. Kyler Murray, Geno Smith and Deshaun Watson are the caliber of names that could be options. Do any of them elevate this team or give the Colts much more than a bridge option?

You can forget about trading for Lamar Jackson. The Colts don't have the assets to compete. That holds true for any other potential starting QB who could be available via trade.

The pathways to salvation appear quite limited. The head coach appears to be on thin ice. The Colts sunk major money into Taylor and Alec Pierce this offseason but have little to show for it.

In short, the whole situation is a hot mess.

articles.title: Patriots' A.J. Brown reportedly expected to be out multiple weeks with hamstring injury
articles.summary: Brown has been limited to four games this season due to a high ankle sprain and strained knee.
articles.body:
New England Patriots receiver A.J. Brown is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks due to a hamstring injury, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter .

Brown, 29, injured his hamstring during Week 10's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. He got hurt in the fourth quarter and did not return, finishing with two catches (on six targets) for 27 yards.

In his first season with the Patriots, Brown has already missed six of the team's 10 games. First, he sustained a high ankle sprain in the season opener and sat out four games while on injured reserve . Then he was sidelined for an additional two games due to a strained knee.

The news on Brown comes as the Patriots also officially announced that quarterback Drake Maye suffered a fractured right fibula against the Lions and could miss the remainder of the regular season.

New England dropped to 5-5 following the defeat versus Detroit and has lost three of its past four games . The Patriots have a bye for Week 11, then visit the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) in Week 12. New England is still in the AFC playoff race , just one game behind the Cleveland Browns (6-4) for the conference's third wild-card berth.

With Brown injured, the Patriots' receiver depth chart consists of Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. Romeo Doubs could join them after the bye week when he's eligible to be activated from IR. Douglas is the team's leading pass-catcher among wideouts with 32 receptions for 438 yards and four touchdowns.

Brown was acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles during the offseason , trading a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-round selection. He registered 1,003 receiving yards last season with the Eagles (his lowest total in four seasons). However, Brown had reportedly become frustrated with quarterback Jalen Hurts — and his role in the Eagles' offense.

Philadelphia traded Brown before a three-year, $96 million extension kicked in that takes him through the 2029 season.

Brown is in his eighth NFL season, beginning his career with the Tennessee Titans. He was the team's second-round selection (No. 51 overall) out of Ole Miss and played with the team for three seasons.

The 6-foot-1 receiver was dealt to the Eagles during the 2022 NFL Draft for first- and fourth-round picks. He subsequently received a four-year, $100 million extension from Philadelphia.

A three-time Pro Bowler and two-time second-team All-Pro selection, Brown has 535 career receptions for 8,157 yards and 56 touchdowns.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker, Baker Mayfield, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 11
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will be without Kenneth Walker for the second straight week.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will be without Kenneth Walker for the second straight week.

The star running back was ruled out of Week 11's matchup with the Arizona Cardinals due to the groin injury that kept him out last week.

Walker's absence is a big blow in fantasy football circles because of the numbers he could've produced against the Arizona defense, but the Chiefs have the bigger picture in view with the Buffalo Bills coming up on Thanksgiving Day.

There's better news regarding Baker Mayfield's health, though, as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is "trending" in the right direction ahead of their battle with the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

Below is a look at all of the significant injuries affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 11.

Kenneth Walker Out For Second Straight Week

The Kansas City Chiefs will have to manage without Kenneth Walker for the second straight week.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid did note on Friday that Walker is "improving" along with a few other injured Chiefs with Thanksgiving Day rapidly approaching.

Emmett Johnson ran for 110 yards, picked up 70 more yards through the air and caught a pair of touchdown passes in place of Walker in Week 10.

It's not crazy to think Johnson will produce at a similar rate in Week 11 given the matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.

The Los Angeles Rams ran for 202 yards on the Cardinals defense in Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks put up 120 rushing yards as a team in Week 9 versus Arizona.

The problem for most fantasy football players is that Johnson is no longer available off the waiver wire because of his wildly successful Week 10.

It's even harder to navigate the waiver wire in Week 11 than most weeks because six teams, including the Detroit Lions and Atlanta Falcons, are on byes.

Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans is a fascinating add for Week 11 because he faces the Dallas Cowboys' league-worst rushing defense. It's also a game against his former team for Pollard.

The Denver Broncos' Jonah Coleman is worth a look as well. He had 57 yards on 17 carries last week and goes up against a Las Vegas Raiders defense that gives up 151.1 rushing yards per game.

Baker Mayfield "Trending In Right Direction"

There's hope in Tampa that Baker Mayfield can play against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles noted on Friday that Mayfield is "trending in the right direction"

Mayfield had plenty of time to rest during Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye ahead of an important two-game stretch for the Bucs. They face the Carolina Panthers on Monday night in Week 12 in a massive NFC South clash.

Mayfield put up 243 passing yards in Week 9 in a tough matchup with the Chicago Bears. He has another difficult matchup on his hands against a Detroit defense that improved over the last month.

The Lions won't have Aidan Hutchinson rushing the quarterback, but they still have all of the key pieces in place in the secondary. That unit allowed under 200 passing yards in each of the last three games.

There aren't many options off the waiver wire if you'd like to sit Mayfield because of the matchup.

Joe Milton of the Philadelphia Eagles is a super sleeper, but he is going up against a Pittsburgh Steelers defense that gives up the third-most passing yards per game.

Cam Ward is an option, too, because of Dallas' propensity to give up high scoring totals. The Titans will likely be playing from behind in that game as well, another positive for Ward's fantasy stock.

articles.title: Patriots' QB Maye could miss rest of the season after injury in Munich
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time after tests indicated that he fractured his right fibula, NFL Insider Adam Schefter said...
articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time after tests indicated that he fractured his right fibula, NFL Insider Adam Schefter said on Friday.

The injury won't require surgery, but is expected to sideline Maye deep into the regular season. A return this year at all is also questionable.

Maye suffered the injury during the Patriots' first offensive drive of their game against the Detroit Lions in Munich last Sunday when sacked by Aidan Hutchinson.

Hutchinson, meanwhile, is set to miss the rest of the season after tearing knee ligaments while celebrating the sack.

articles.title: NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games
articles.summary: After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question o...
articles.body:
After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question of whether the league should require teams to get there early enough to advance the goal of promoting American football to international audiences.

Via The Athletic , the NFL will consider adopting a minimum-night stay for teams playing internationally.

"Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O'Reilly told The Athletic . "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at."

The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual "Opening Night" media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities.

"Having access to players and that type of experience when they're in the market does have a lasting impact," O'Reilly said. "That's a factor when you start to think about encouraging or potentially looking at a policy where you'd want a club in the market for more than the day before."

Beyond impacting strategic considerations, it would add to the total expense. The money would be worth it, if it further enhances the league's overall reason for going global.
